name: Berlandiera

project_scope.taxonomy_hold: B. betonicifolia may be treated as a hybrid or under B. texana; verify before species installation.

look_here_first: Compare mature leaves and stem leafiness, then turn a composite head sideways to see the broad overlapping phyllaries.
shared_genus_traits: Composite heads with yellow ray florets, dark disk florets and conspicuous phyllaries.
Perennial herbs with alternate leaves; shapes vary by species.

species_comparison_matrix.betonicifolia: Broad toothed triangular-ovate leaves on erect leafy stems.
species_comparison_matrix.lyrata: Often lyrate basal leaves with smaller lateral lobes.
species_comparison_matrix.how_to_check: Photograph mature leaves and whole stem with scale.

species_comparison_matrix.betonicifolia: Yellow rays, dark disk, broad phyllaries.
species_comparison_matrix.lyrata: Yellow rays, dark disk, broad phyllaries.
species_comparison_matrix.how_to_check: Same-scale head front and underside; genus clue not species separator.

shared_structure_examples.plain: Green bracts under a flower head.
Many small flowers compose one head.
One large end lobe and smaller side lobes.
shared_structure_examples.photo_role: mature leaf and node with ruler

shared_structure_examples.plain: A small dry fruit produced by one floret of the composite head.
shared_structure_examples.photo_role: mature disk-head fruit macro with scale

study_strategy.warning: B. betonicifolia concept unresolved; do not certify native status.
look_here_first: Find a whole flowering shoot and distinguish basal from stem leaves.
Compare mature leaf lobes, teeth and petiole at matched scale.
Turn a flower head sideways to inspect overlapping phyllaries; separate ray from disk florets.
Inspect mature cypselae before finalizing a difficult specimen.

comparison_cards.title: B. betonicifolia versus B. lyrata
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Compare broad toothed stem leaves versus often lyrate basal leaves.
comparison_cards.caution: Taxonomy of B. betonicifolia requires review.

comparison_cards.title: Berlandiera versus similar yellow-headed asters
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Look below the head at phyllaries, compare leaf arrangement and division, then inspect mature fruits; yellow rays alone do not establish genus.
comparison_cards.caution: Do not use chocolate scent or disk color as a decisive character; exact local look-alike keys need botanical review.

curation_status.visual_status: four specific structural lessons, no verified installed species photos; taxonomy hold retained

part_examples.title: 1 · Basal and stem leaves
part_examples.look_for: B. lyrata may show a larger end lobe with smaller lateral lobes (lyrate); compare with toothed broad leaves in the unresolved B. betonicifolia concept.
part_examples.why_it_matters: Leaf division is more useful than shared yellow rays.

part_examples.title: 2 · Ray and disk florets
part_examples.look_for: Outer ray florets and central disk florets are separate flowers in one composite head.
part_examples.why_it_matters: Teaches the Asteraceae architecture shared by both source concepts.

part_examples.title: 3 · Phyllaries beneath the head
part_examples.look_for: Turn the flower head sideways and locate the overlapping green bracts (phyllaries).
part_examples.why_it_matters: A structural genus clue and a safeguard against flower-color identification.

part_examples.title: 4 · Mature cypselae
part_examples.role: dry fruit macro with millimeter scale
part_examples.look_for: Photograph mature dry fruits from the head; verify shape and pappus before labeling.
part_examples.why_it_matters: Adds a reproductive character for future diagnostic confirmation.
